title: A Flower for the Shopkeeper
learning_objectives: Explain the reasons for Sam and Grandma's small acts of kindness.
Compare the two uses of paper bags in the story.
parent_prompts: Before reading: The title names a gift for a shopkeeper. What could someone want to thank a shopkeeper for?
After page 5: Why does Grandma want to buy a flower? How is her reason different from Sam's reason for holding the bag?
After reading: Compare the bag carrying tomatoes with the bag decorating the jar. What holds the flower and water? Why is Sam glad?

quiz.prompt: How are Sam's and Grandma's reasons different?

options.text: Sam thanks her; Grandma needs help
Sam helps; Grandma thanks past kindness
Both thank her for today's packing

quiz.explanation: Page 3 says Sam wants to help with packing now. Page 5 says Grandma wants to thank the shopkeeper for saving her favorite tomatoes every visit.

quiz.prompt: Why does Sam carry a flower back after shopping?

options.text: To trade it for more tomatoes

quiz.explanation: Page 5 says Grandma wants to thank the shopkeeper for saving her favorite tomatoes. On page 6, Grandma buys the flower and Sam carries it back.

quiz.prompt: Why does Grandma's gift belong in this story?

options.text: It returns kindness from earlier visits
It thanks Sam for holding the bag

quiz.explanation: Grandma remembers the shopkeeper saving her favorite tomatoes on every visit (page 5), buys a flower (page 6), and leaves a gift the shopkeeper can enjoy (page 8). The gift returns earlier kindness.

quiz.prompt: Compare the bag carrying tomatoes with the bag around the jar. Why does Sam smile when he leaves?
quiz.rubric: not yet: names the tomatoes or flower without explaining either bag use; with support: describes a bag carrying tomatoes or decorating the jar; independent: contrasts carrying tomatoes with decorating the water jar, identifies the jar as the flower holder, and connects Sam's smile to the shopkeeper enjoying their gift
quiz.explanation: Pages 3 and 4 show a bag holding tomatoes for carrying. On page 7, another bag decorates a jar; the jar holds the water and flower. Page 8 says Sam is glad the shopkeeper can enjoy their gift.

activities.prompt: Put the helping and thanking moments in story order.

items.text: Sam wraps a paper bag around the jar.

prompts: Grandma remembers the tomatoes the shopkeeper saves. How can remembering a kindness change what someone does next?
What earlier kindness might the shopkeeper remember when she sees the flower in its decorated jar? Use an event from the book.

off_screen_prompt: Make a pretend market with three household objects. Take turns being a shopper and shopkeeper, and invent a small thank you for something your partner does.
